notes: Access: www.harrods.com is Akamai-WAF-protected; curl_cffi impersonate='safari17_0' bypassed it cleanly (HTTP 200) for every URL fetched (per notes/276.md). Scope: Home & Furniture department only, discovered from the Home dept mega-menu on https://www.harrods.com/en-gb/c/departments/home-and-furniture. Checked: main nav / Home department flyout menu (all columns: Living Room, Kitchen & Dining, New & Exclusives, etc.), footer, root homepage top nav, and direct URL guesses (/en-gb/home-bestsellers, /en-gb/home-best-sellers, /en-gb/best-sellers-home, /en-gb/trending-home, /en-gb/home-trending, /en-gb/popular-homeware, /en-gb/most-popular-home - all 404). No page literally named 'Bestsellers'/'Best Sellers'/'Top Sellers' exists for Home. The site's genuine equivalent merchandising concept for Home is 'Trending Homeware' (https://www.harrods.com/en-gb/trending-homeware), linked directly in the Home department mega-menu alongside 'New In'; title tag 'Trending Homeware | Harrods UK', meta description 'Shop trending homeware at Harrods.' Confirmed as a real PLP: has Sort by / Filter controls and a genuine product grid (not editorial). This matches the brief's target term 'Trending Products'/'Popular Products'. Other departments (Women/Men/Beauty/Jewellery) expose actual '<dept>-bestsellers' URLs (e.g. /en-gb/women-bestsellers) but Home does not have a 'home-bestsellers' equivalent - Trending Homeware is the closest and only genuine popularity-merchandising PLP found for this department. No further sub-structure (e.g. 'Furniture Bestsellers') exists in the nav - only this single undifferentiated listing.
